newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich says will negotiate tax bill with Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich says will negotiate tax bill with Clinton.

text.p: U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich on Friday said Republicans will have to negotiate with President Clinton to get a tax bill he will sign, but said that did not mean they would accept a major rewrite of the bill.
"We will sit down with the president's folks and with the president and try to reach an accommodation on issues of great importance to the president," Gingrich told reporters.
But he said that, as long as the bill met the overall agreement with Clinton, "I don't think we have an obligation" to let the White House rewrite the bill.
The House Ways and Means Committee after a marathon session on strict party lines approved a bill to cut taxes by $85 billion over five years.

Gingrich said he expected the measure would pass the House, adding: "There's a lot in that bill and I'm not sure how many Democrats on final passage...are going to want to go home and say I voted against every single tax break that you wanted.
"If the president wants to veto the first tax cut in 16 years, that's his prerogative."
